You are a credit analyst deciding which extracted facts belong in a credit-review report used to size a credit line for a borrower. Keep facts that bear on repayment capacity, leverage, liquidity, credit history, ratings, governance, litigation, or industry risk. Always keep dividends declared or recommended (even by a loss-making company), buybacks and other cash outflows, and any item that the scoring-policy slot descriptions mention. Drop boilerplate, marketing language, and trivia, and administrative lines such as book closure, record date, IEPF and e-payment instructions. Use dup only for a repeat of the same fact from the same document; a repeat in a different document is a second citation, so keep it (code merges duplicates afterwards). Use stale only when the notebook shows a newer equivalent entry for a later period.

The bank's scoring policy needs these inputs. Always keep an entry that states any of them (including a derived figure, a rating index or a red-flag count), even if it seems minor, a repeat, or forward-looking:
- net_debt: Total borrowings less cash, bank balances and liquid investments, latest audited year
- ebitda: Operating profit before depreciation, interest and tax, excluding other income
- interest_expense: Gross finance cost for the year
- cfads: Cash flow available for debt service: EBITDA less cash taxes paid
- debt_service: Interest paid plus scheduled principal repayments in the year
- total_debt: Total borrowings (short and long term, including current maturities and leases)
- total_equity: Shareholders' equity (net worth) at year end
- current_assets: Total current assets at year end
- current_liabilities: Total current liabilities at year end
- revenue_current: Revenue from operations, latest audited year
- revenue_previous: Revenue from operations, previous audited year
- external_rating_index: Bank numeric index of the latest long-term external rating: AAA=1, AA+=2, ... BBB-=10, BB+=11, ... D=22
- major_red_flag_count: Number of major red flags present under policy section 6
- default_flag: 1 if any NPA, wilful default or one-time settlement in the last 36 months, else 0
- proposed_exposure: Proposed aggregate bank exposure including existing limits
- projected_turnover: Projected annual turnover for the next financial year
- tangible_net_worth: Tangible net worth at year end

API Business :
The API division continued to strengthen its position as a reliable supplier of APIs to global generic
pharmaceutical companies while supporting the Company’s formulation business through the supply
of high-quality captive APIs. During FY 2025-26, the division delivered strong operational and
commercial performance despite a challenging global business environment.
External API sales increased primarily driven by higher demand for ophthalmic, anti-gout and anti-
diabetic APIs, supported by new customer approvals, increased volumes from existing customers and
a favourable product mix.
During the year, Indoco’s API facility at Patalganga successfully completed USFDA inspection without
any observations (No Form 483 issued). This milestone reinforces the Company’s commitment to
world-class quality systems and strengthens customer confidence, particularly in the regulated markets.
Europe remained the division’s largest export market during the year, while demand from India and
other emerging markets continued to strengthen. Growth was primarily driven by increased sales of
ophthalmic, anti-gout and anti-diabetic APIs.
With a strong customer pipeline, enhanced manufacturing capacity, robust regulatory compliance and
a diversified product portfolio, the division is well positioned to capitalize on emerging opportunities
and deliver sustainable growth in the coming years.

Indoco Remedies Limited (the Company) is a Public Limited Company domiciled in India and incorporated under the
provision of the Companies Act, VII of 1913. Its Shares are listed on two stock exchanges in India i.e Bombay Stock
Exchange and National Stock Exchange. Indoco Remedies Limited is engaged in the manufacturing and marketing
of Formulations (Finished Dosage Forms) and Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs). The Company caters to both
Domestic and International markets. Company has four wholly owned subsidiaries, Xtend Industrial Designers and
Engineers Pvt. Ltd. (formerly known as Indoco Industrial Designers & Engineers Pvt. Ltd.) , Indoco Remedies Czech
sro, Indoco Remedies UK Limited & Warren Remedies Private Limited. The Company has acquired 85% equity stake
in FPP Holding Company, LLC a company registered in Delaware, USA on June 5, 2023.
1.
Material Accounting Policies followed by the Company
a)
Basis of Preparation
(i) 	 Compliance with Ind AS
These financial statements have been prepared in accordance with the Indian Accounting Standards
(hereinafter referred to as the ‘Ind AS’) as notified by Ministry of Corporate Affairs pursuant to Section
133 of the Companies Act, 2013 (‘Act’) read with of the Companies (Indian Accounting Standards)
Rules, 2015 as amended and other relevant provisions of the Act.
These standalone financial statements were authorised for issue by the Company’s Board of Directors
on May 07, 2026.
(ii)	 Historical cost convention
The financial statements have been prepared on a historical cost basis, except for the following:
•
Certain financial assets and liabilities that are measured at fair value;
•
Defined benefit plans - Plan assets measured at fair value;
•
Assets held for sale – measured at fair value less cost to sell;
(iii)	 Current non-current classification
All assets and liabilities have been classified as current or non-current as per the Company’s normal
operating cycle (twelve months) and other criteria set out in Schedule III to the Act.
(iv)	 Rounding of amounts
All amounts disclosed in the financial statements and notes have been rounded off to the nearest lakhs
as per the requirement of Schedule III, unless otherwise stated.
b)
Use of estimates and judgements
The preparation of financial statements requires management of the Company to make estimates and
assumptions that affect the reported assets and liabilities, revenue and expenses and disclosures relating
to contingent liabilities. Management believes that the estimates used in the preparation of the financial
statements are prudent and reasonable. Management at each reporting date reviews estimates and
underlying assumptions. Actual results could differ from these estimates. Any revision of these estimates is
recognised prospectively in the current and future periods.

Taxes on Income:

on whether tax positions are probable of being sustained in tax assessments. A tax assessment can

Notes (Standalone)
on financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2026

Note: 52 - FINANCIAL RISK MANAGEMENT
Financial risk management objectives and policies
The Company’s financial risk management is an integral part of how to plan and execute its business strategies. The
Company’s financial risk management policy is set by the Audit Committee of the Board of Director.
Market risk is the risk of loss of future earnings, fair values or future cash flows that may result from a change in
the price of a financial instrument. The value of a financial instrument may change as a result of changes in the
interest rates, foreign currency exchange rates, equity prices and other market changes that affect market risk sensitive
instruments. Market risk is attributable to all market risk sensitive financial instruments including investments and
deposits, foreign currency receivables, payables and loans and borrowings.
The Company manages market risk through a Finance department, which evaluates and exercises independent
control over the entire process of market risk management. The Finance department recommend the risk management
objectives and policies, which are approved by Senior Management and the Audit Committee. The activities of this
department include management of cash resources, implementing hedging strategies for foreign currency exposures
like foreign exchange forward contracts, borrowing strategies and ensuring compliance with market risk limits and
policies.
Market Risk- Interest rate risk
Interest rate risk is the risk that the fair value of future cash flows of the financial instruments will fluctuate because
of changes in market interest rates. In order to optimize the Company’s position with regards to interest income
and interest expenses and to manage the interest rate risk, finance department performs a comprehensive corporate
interest rate risk management policy by balancing the proportion of fixed rate and floating rate financial instruments
in its total portfolio.
According to the Company interest rate risk exposure is only for floating rate borrowings. For floating rate liabilities,
the analysis is prepared assuming the amount of liability outstanding at the end of the reporting period was outstanding
for the whole year. 50-basis point increase or decrease is used when reporting interest rate risk internally to key
management personnel and represents management’s assessment of the reasonably possible change in interest rates.

Independent Auditors’ Report (Consolidated)
to the Members of Indoco Remedies Limited
Report on the Audit of Consolidated Financial Statements
Opinion
We have audited the accompanying consolidated financial statements of INDOCO REMEDIES LIMITED
(“the Holding Company”) and its subsidiaries (collectively referred to as “the Group”), which comprise
the consolidated Balance Sheet as at March 31, 2026, and the consolidated Statement of Profit and Loss
(including Other Comprehensive Income), Consolidated Cash Flow Statement and the Consolidated
Statement of Changes in Equity for the year ended and notes to the consolidated financial statements
(including summary of material accounting policies) and other explanatory information (hereinafter
referred to as “the consolidated financial statements”).
In our opinion and to the best of our information and according to the explanations given to us, the
aforesaid consolidated financial statements give the information required by the Companies Act, 2013
(“the Act”) in the manner so required and give a true and fair view in conformity with the Indian Accounting
Standards prescribed under section 133 of the Act read with the Companies (Indian Accounting Standards)
Rules, 2015, as amended, (“Ind AS”) and other accounting principles generally accepted in India, of the
consolidated state of affairs of the Group as at March 31, 2026, and its consolidated Loss and consolidated
total comprehensive income, its consolidated changes in equity and its consolidated cash inflows for the
year ended on that date.
Basis for Opinion
We conducted our audit of the consolidated financial statements in accordance with the Standards on
Auditing (SAs) specified under section 143(10) of the Act. Our responsibilities under those Standards are
further described in the Auditor’s Responsibilities for the Audit of the Consolidated Financial Statements
section of our report. We are independent of the Group in accordance with the Code of Ethics issued by
the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India together with the ethical requirements that are relevant to
our audit of the consolidated financial statements under the provisions of the Act and the Rules thereunder,
and we have fulfilled our other ethical responsibilities in accordance with these requirements and the
Code of Ethics. We believe that the audit evidence we have obtained is sufficient and appropriate to
provide a basis for our opinion.
Emphasis of Matter
We draw attention to the Note on Non-current Financial Investment in Consolidated financial statements -
A)
FPP Holding LLC
The Company incurred a net loss ` 2,365.21 Lakhs during the year ended March 31, 2026. As at that
date, the Company has a negative networth of ` 4,225.11 Lakhs.
The above condition indicate the existence of a material uncertainty that may cast significant doubt
on the ability of the respective company to continue as going concern. In accordance with the
requirements of Ind AS 36, Impairment of Assets, the Group has carried out impairment testing of
the carrying amounts of its investments in these subsidiaries, given the erosion of their net worth.
Based on the impairment assessment performed by management, which included review of long-
term business plans, cash flow forecasts, and other relevant assumptions, the recoverable amounts
of these investments were estimated to exceed their respective carrying values. Accordingly, no
impairment provision has been considered necessary by the management at this stage.

Note 54 : FINANCIAL RISK MANAGEMENT
Financial risk management objectives and policies
The Company’s financial risk management is an integral part of how to plan and execute its business strategies. The
Company’s financial risk management policy is set by the Audit Committee of the Board of Director.
Market risk is the risk of loss of future earnings, fair values or future cash flows that may result from a change in
the price of a financial instrument. The value of a financial instrument may change as a result of changes in the
interest rates, foreign currency exchange rates, equity prices and other market changes that affect market risk sensitive
instruments. Market risk is attributable to all market risk sensitive financial instruments including investments and
deposits, foreign currency receivables, payables and loans and borrowings.
The Company manages market risk through a Finance department, which evaluates and exercises independent
control over the entire process of market risk management. The Finance department recommend the risk management
objectives and policies, which are approved by Senior Management and the Audit Committee. The activities of this
department include management of cash resources, implementing hedging strategies for foreign currency exposures
like foreign exchange forward contracts, borrowing strategies and ensuring compliance with market risk limits and
policies.
Market Risk- Interest rate risk
Interest rate risk is the risk that the fair value of future cash flows of the financial instruments will fluctuate because
of changes in market interest rates. In order to optimize the Company’s position with regards to interest income
and interest expenses and to manage the interest rate risk, finance department performs a comprehensive corporate
interest rate risk management policy by balancing the proportion of fixed rate and floating rate financial instruments
in its total portfolio.
According to the Company interest rate risk exposure is only for floating rate borrowings. For floating rate liabilities,
the analysis is prepared assuming the amount of the liability outstanding at the end of the reporting period was
outstanding for the whole year. A 50 basis point increase or decrease is used when reporting interest rate risk internally
to key management personnel and represents management’s assessment of the reasonably possible change in interest
rates.

The Company’s financial risk management is an integral part of how to plan and execute its business strategies. The

Market risk is the risk of loss of future earnings, fair values or future cash flows that may result from a change in
the price of a financial instrument. The value of a financial instrument may change as a result of changes in the

policies.

of changes in market interest rates. In order to optimize the Company’s position with regards to interest income

interest rate risk management policy by balancing the proportion of fixed rate and floating rate financial instruments

Rationale
The rating reaffirmation and the continuation of the negative outlook on the long-term rating take into account the deterioration
in Indoco Remedies Limited’s (IRL/ the company) revenues, operating net profit margins and debt metrics in FY2025 and the
company’s continued weak performance in Q1 FY2026. ICRA expects the company’s debt metrics to remain impacted in FY2026
by high debt levels. The company’s performance was weaker-than-expected in FY2025 and Q1 FY2026, primarily due to supply-
side disruptions caused by the ongoing refurbishment of its manufacturing plants as part of its master manufacturing plan (MMP)
and the ongoing remediation for its Goa facility. This impacted its sales to export markets, leading to a contraction in IRL’s
operating margins. Further, the company’s continued investments in the over the counter (OTC)toothpaste segment have also
impacted the margins to a certain extent.
While the company’s total debt has reduced marginally to around Rs. 952 crore as on June 30, 2025 over Rs. 994 crore as on
March 31, 2025, it remains elevated compared to Rs. 672 crore as on March 31, 2024. The increase was primarily driven by the
ongoing capex for refurbishing manufacturing plants in Goa, Waluj (Maharashtra) and Baddi (Himachal Pradesh), additional lines
at Sterile site in Goa and fast-tracked debt-funded capex in its wholly-owned subsidiary, Warren Remedies Limited, to establish
facilities for toothpaste and active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) manufacturing. Overall, the company availed additional debt
of about Rs. 264.3 crore in FY2025. Along with deterioration in operating profit margin (OPM) to 6.0% in FY2025 from 13.4% in
FY2024, this resulted in a deterioration in its debt metrics.
The ratings, however, continue to draw comfort from IRL’s established position in the domestic formulation segment and its
diversified geographic presence.

Rationale
The rating reaffirmation and the continuation of the negative outlook on the long-term rating take into account the deterioration
in Indoco Remedies Limited’s (IRL/ the company) revenues, operating net profit margins and debt metrics in FY2025 and the
company’s continued weak performance in Q1 FY2026. ICRA expects the company’s debt metrics to remain impacted in FY2026
by high debt levels. The company’s performance was weaker-than-expected in FY2025 and Q1 FY2026, primarily due to supply-
side disruptions caused by the ongoing refurbishment of its manufacturing plants as part of its master manufacturing plan (MMP)
and the ongoing remediation for its Goa facility. This impacted its sales to export markets, leading to a contraction in IRL’s
operating margins. Further, the company’s continued investments in the over the counter (OTC)toothpaste segment have also
impacted the margins to a certain extent.
While the company’s total debt has reduced marginally to around Rs. 952 crore as on June 30, 2025 over Rs. 994 crore as on
March 31, 2025, it remains elevated compared to Rs. 672 crore as on March 31, 2024. The increase was primarily driven by the
ongoing capex for refurbishing manufacturing plants in Goa, Waluj (Maharashtra) and Baddi (Himachal Pradesh), additional lines
at Sterile site in Goa and fast-tracked debt-funded capex in its wholly-owned subsidiary, Warren Remedies Limited, to establish
facilities for toothpaste and active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) manufacturing. Overall, the company availed additional debt
of about Rs. 264.3 crore in FY2025. Along with deterioration in operating profit margin (OPM) to 6.0% in FY2025 from 13.4% in
FY2024, this resulted in a deterioration in its debt metrics.
The ratings, however, continue to draw comfort from IRL’s established position in the domestic formulation segment and its
diversified geographic presence.

Statement:
Any new Abbreviated New Drug Application (ANDA) filings from the Goa Plants II and III facility will be approved only when the OAI status is resolved.

Source passage:
and ophthalmology. The segment also benefited from extension of lifespan for some of its legacy products such as Cital-PM6
solution, Nosic OD, and Ezetrol in Q1 FY2026. Going forward, the domestic market is expected to render stable revenue growth
for IRL in FY2026 and FY2027, supported by its strong market position in respective therapy segments.
Healthy geographic diversification – In FY2025 and Q1 FY2026, although the company witnessed a revenue decline in export
formulations, it was partially offset by revenue growth in domestic formulations. IRL derived around 90% of its sales revenue
in Q1 FY2026 from the formulation segment, with 53% of the segment’s revenues generated by domestic markets and the rest
from export markets. The company has a strong domestic presence, with its major brands positioned among the top five in
respective therapy segments. In terms of export markets, regulated markets such as the US, Europe, South Africa, Australia
and New Zealand generated 68% of its export formulation revenues, while the rest came from the emerging markets. Going
forward, the revenues are expected to remain diversified, with stable growth from domestic markets and an expected gradual
revival in revenues from key export markets.
Credit challenges
Pending resolution of OAI status from the USFDA for IRL’s Goa Plants II and III – IRL’s Goa Plants II and III were inspected by
USFDA in February 2023 and received their OAI status in June 2023. While IRL was working on the remediation, USFDA audited
the facility again in February 2024 and a warning letter was issued to the site in December 2024. IRL is working on remediating
the same, and its US revenues from the site were impacted to some extent due to the ongoing refurbishment. USFDA has given
approval for resumption of production for two lines of the four at the Goa Plant II recently. ICRA notes that the manufacturing
facility for Oral Solid Dosage (OSD) at Goa Plant I continues to remain Current Good Manufacturing Practice (CGMP) compliant
and supply to the US continues from this site. Going forward, any new Abbreviated New Drug Application (ANDA) filings from
the facility will be approved only when the OAI status is resolved and, hence, timely resolution of the same remains a key
monitorable.
Vulnerability to regulatory risks, raw material price and foreign exchange fluctuations – The company’s operations remain
exposed to regulatory risks due to increased scrutiny by the regulatory agencies and pricing controls in the domestic market.
ICRA notes that the company derives some revenues from products under the National List of Essential Medicines (NLEM) but
draws comfort from the fact that the same has not materially impacted its profit margins. Nevertheless, any adverse changes
in Government price policies could lead to pricing pressures and affect the company’s domestic formulations business. IRL’s
profitability is also vulnerable to fluctuations in raw material, packaging and freight costs and their impact on margins will
remain a key monitorable. The company’s margins also remain vulnerable to foreign exchange fluctuations due to its overseas
operations and foreign currency borrowings despite hedging through forward contracts. ICRA notes that IRL capitalises
development expenditures for ANDAs/Drug Master Files (DMFs)/dossiers and any higher-than-expected price erosion or
lower-than-expected returns, exposes the company to the risk of impairment of intangibles.

and ophthalmology. The segment also benefited from extension of lifespan for some of its legacy products such as Cital-PM6

for IRL in FY2026 and FY2027, supported by its strong market position in respective therapy segments.
Healthy geographic diversification – In FY2025 and Q1 FY2026, although the company witnessed a revenue decline in export
formulations, it was partially offset by revenue growth in domestic formulations. IRL derived around 90% of its sales revenue
in Q1 FY2026 from the formulation segment, with 53% of the segment’s revenues generated by domestic markets and the rest
from export markets. The company has a strong domestic presence, with its major brands positioned among the top five in
respective therapy segments. In terms of export markets, regulated markets such as the US, Europe, South Africa, Australia
and New Zealand generated 68% of its export formulation revenues, while the rest came from the emerging markets. Going
forward, the revenues are expected to remain diversified, with stable growth from domestic markets and an expected gradual
revival in revenues from key export markets.
Credit challenges
Pending resolution of OAI status from the USFDA for IRL’s Goa Plants II and III – IRL’s Goa Plants II and III were inspected by
USFDA in February 2023 and received their OAI status in June 2023. While IRL was working on the remediation, USFDA audited
the facility again in February 2024 and a warning letter was issued to the site in December 2024. IRL is working on remediating
the same, and its US revenues from the site were impacted to some extent due to the ongoing refurbishment. USFDA has given
approval for resumption of production for two lines of the four at the Goa Plant II recently. ICRA notes that the manufacturing
facility for Oral Solid Dosage (OSD) at Goa Plant I continues to remain Current Good Manufacturing Practice (CGMP) compliant
and supply to the US continues from this site. Going forward, any new Abbreviated New Drug Application (ANDA) filings from
the facility will be approved only when the OAI status is resolved and, hence, timely resolution of the same remains a key
monitorable.
Vulnerability to regulatory risks, raw material price and foreign exchange fluctuations – The company’s operations remain
exposed to regulatory risks due to increased scrutiny by the regulatory agencies and pricing controls in the domestic market.
ICRA notes that the company derives some revenues from products under the National List of Essential Medicines (NLEM) but
draws comfort from the fact that the same has not materially impacted its profit margins. Nevertheless, any adverse changes
in Government price policies could lead to pricing pressures and affect the company’s domestic formulations business. IRL’s
profitability is also vulnerable to fluctuations in raw material, packaging and freight costs and their impact on margins will
remain a key monitorable. The company’s margins also remain vulnerable to foreign exchange fluctuations due to its overseas
operations and foreign currency borrowings despite hedging through forward contracts. ICRA notes that IRL capitalises
development expenditures for ANDAs/Drug Master Files (DMFs)/dossiers and any higher-than-expected price erosion or
lower-than-expected returns, exposes the company to the risk of impairment of intangibles.

Increasing working capital intensity of operations – The company’s working capital intensity was moderately high at 37.7% in
FY2025 and 34.0% in FY2024. For domestic sales, it typically offers a credit period of 7–90 days and for export sales, debtor
days range from 30–120 days. The company’s revenue from export markets (primarily in formulations) are working capital
intensive and resulted in a moderate rise in inventory days. IRL encountered regulatory issues during FY2018-FY2019, leading
to stretched payable days in FY2019. However, after the resolution of these issues and with improving cash accruals, IRL
substantially reduced its creditor days. Consequently, the working capital intensity has increased since then. Going forward,
as the company continues to focus on export markets, its working capital intensity is likely to remain in line with recent trends.
Sizeable debt-funded capex – While the company’s total debt level has reduced marginally to around Rs. 952 crore as on June
30, 2025 over Rs. 994 crore as on March 31, 2025 it remains elevated compared to Rs. 672 crore as on March 31, 2024. The
increase was primarily driven by the ongoing capex for refurbishing manufacturing plants in Goa and Baddi, and fast-tracked
debt-funded capex in its wholly-owned subsidiary, Warren Remedies Limited, to establish facilities for toothpaste and API
manufacturing. Overall, the company availed additional debt of about Rs. 264.3 crore in FY2025.

Statement:
The company's liquidity position remains adequate with free cash and liquid investments of Rs. 15.76 crore as on June 30, 2025.

Source passage:
2024. The rise in debt levels, combined with reduced operating margin, affected the coverage indicators as well, with the
interest coverage ratio declining to 1.5 times in FY2025 from 6.4 times in FY2024. The interest coverage declined further to 0.7
times in Q1 FY2026 due to elevated interest; although interest costs included mark-to-market losses of around Rs. 7.4 crore,
which are notional in nature. The company is estimated to incur capex of Rs. 50-60 crore each in FY2026 and FY2027. Going
forward, stable performance in the domestic market supported by a revival in sales in key export markets and significant
expansion in operating margins remain crucial for the improvement in IRL’s debt metrics.
Environmental and Social Risks
Environmental considerations – The company does not face any major physical climate risk. However, it remains exposed to
tightening environmental regulations with regard to breach of waste and pollution norms, which can lead to an increase in
operating costs or capital investments. To address this, the company is dedicated to minimising its environmental footprint by
continuously improving its operations, reducing its energy consumption, and managing its waste and emissions responsibly.
IRL has recently installed solar power plants at two of its facilities and is planning to install more at other locations.
Social considerations – The industry faces social risks related to product safety and the associated litigation risks, access to
qualified personnel for R&D and process engineering and maintenance of high manufacturing compliance standards. Further,
Government intervention related to price caps/control also remains a social risk faced by entities in the pharmaceutical
industry. The company is committed to promoting the health and safety of its employees by providing a safe work
environment, supporting a culture of wellness, and investing in training and development. The company also supports local
initiatives, engages in philanthropic activities and partners with organisations that share its commitment to sustainability and
social responsibility.
Liquidity position: Adequate
The company’s liquidity position remains adequate with free cash and liquid investments of Rs. 15.76 crore as on June 30,
2025. The company’s working capital utilisation remains high, reflected by an average utilisation of 96.5% (against its average
drawing power (DP) of Rs. 346.8 crore) during the 12-month period ended in June 2025. IRL’s capex requirement for FY2026
are to be funded through internal accruals. It has debt servicing obligations of Rs. 68 crore for FY2026 and Rs. 139.4 crore for
FY2027. ICRA expects the company to meet its near-term repayment obligations through its accruals and existing cash
balances.
Rating sensitivities
Positive factors – The outlook may be revised to Stable in case the company demonstrates significant improvement in its
margins, leading to sustained improvement in its debt metrics, return indicators and liquidity position.
Negative factors – The rating may be downgraded if the company is unable to improve its revenues and margins materially by
scaling the additional capacities built over the last three years, leading to further weakening in the company’s overall financial
profile. Delays in resolution of existing regulatory non-compliance or any other regulatory non-compliance, thereby impacting
its product launches and, thus, revenues and profitability, would also be a negative rating trigger.

(CRAMS), with a strong presence in domestic formulations, which generated 53% of its total revenues in Q1 FY2026. In the

Statement:
The company has debt servicing obligations of Rs. 68 crore for FY2026 and Rs. 139.4 crore for FY2027.

Source passage:
2024. The rise in debt levels, combined with reduced operating margin, affected the coverage indicators as well, with the
interest coverage ratio declining to 1.5 times in FY2025 from 6.4 times in FY2024. The interest coverage declined further to 0.7
times in Q1 FY2026 due to elevated interest; although interest costs included mark-to-market losses of around Rs. 7.4 crore,
which are notional in nature. The company is estimated to incur capex of Rs. 50-60 crore each in FY2026 and FY2027. Going
forward, stable performance in the domestic market supported by a revival in sales in key export markets and significant
expansion in operating margins remain crucial for the improvement in IRL’s debt metrics.
Environmental and Social Risks
Environmental considerations – The company does not face any major physical climate risk. However, it remains exposed to
tightening environmental regulations with regard to breach of waste and pollution norms, which can lead to an increase in
operating costs or capital investments. To address this, the company is dedicated to minimising its environmental footprint by
continuously improving its operations, reducing its energy consumption, and managing its waste and emissions responsibly.
IRL has recently installed solar power plants at two of its facilities and is planning to install more at other locations.
Social considerations – The industry faces social risks related to product safety and the associated litigation risks, access to
qualified personnel for R&D and process engineering and maintenance of high manufacturing compliance standards. Further,
Government intervention related to price caps/control also remains a social risk faced by entities in the pharmaceutical
industry. The company is committed to promoting the health and safety of its employees by providing a safe work
environment, supporting a culture of wellness, and investing in training and development. The company also supports local
initiatives, engages in philanthropic activities and partners with organisations that share its commitment to sustainability and
social responsibility.
Liquidity position: Adequate
The company’s liquidity position remains adequate with free cash and liquid investments of Rs. 15.76 crore as on June 30,
2025. The company’s working capital utilisation remains high, reflected by an average utilisation of 96.5% (against its average
drawing power (DP) of Rs. 346.8 crore) during the 12-month period ended in June 2025. IRL’s capex requirement for FY2026
are to be funded through internal accruals. It has debt servicing obligations of Rs. 68 crore for FY2026 and Rs. 139.4 crore for
FY2027. ICRA expects the company to meet its near-term repayment obligations through its accruals and existing cash
balances.
Rating sensitivities
Positive factors – The outlook may be revised to Stable in case the company demonstrates significant improvement in its
margins, leading to sustained improvement in its debt metrics, return indicators and liquidity position.
Negative factors – The rating may be downgraded if the company is unable to improve its revenues and margins materially by
scaling the additional capacities built over the last three years, leading to further weakening in the company’s overall financial
profile. Delays in resolution of existing regulatory non-compliance or any other regulatory non-compliance, thereby impacting
its product launches and, thus, revenues and profitability, would also be a negative rating trigger.

About the company
IRL was established by Mr. Govind Ramnath Kare in 1945 as Indo Continental Trading Company. It was involved in importing
pharmaceutical formulations from Europe and selling them in India. In 1963, the current Chairman and Managing Director,
Mr. Suresh G. Kare took over.
At present, IRL manufactures and markets branded formulations, APIs and contract research and manufacturing services
(CRAMS), with a strong presence in domestic formulations, which generated 53% of its total revenues in Q1 FY2026. In the
domestic business, the company has a prominent presence in the anti-infective, respiratory, gastrointestinal and dental
segments, with its major brands positioned among the top five in their respective categories. Export formulations comprised
36% of IRL’s revenues in Q1 FY2026, while APIs formed 10%, with the rest generated by contract research and analytics
divisions.

API plants are in Patalganga (Maharashtra) and Rabale (Navi Mumbai). The facilities have been approved by most major

#SEBI’s grievance redressal/dispute resolution and SEBI investor protection mechanisms such as SCORES and ODR shall not be available for activities and
instruments, which fall under the regulatory purview of Financial Sector Regulators other than SEBI.
Rationale
The reaffirmation of the ratings and continuation of the Negative outlook on the long-term rating reflect Indoco Remedies
Limited’s (IRL/the company) elevated debt levels, weak debt-protection metrics and moderately high working capital intensity,
despite the recovery in its operating performance in FY2026. The ratings remain constrained by the continued regulatory
overhang at its Goa Plant II and uncertainty regarding the pace and sustainability of improvement in profitability, cash accruals
and leverage. The continued investments in the over-the-counter (OTC) oral care business under Warren Remedies Private
Limited have also constrained the company’s consolidated profitability in FY2026. While the completion of major plant
modifications under the Master Manufacturing Plan (MMP) and the liquidity infusion through recent asset monetisation
initiatives provide some comfort, a sustained improvement in operating performance and its translation into stronger cash
accruals, improvement in debt protection metrics and meaningful deleveraging remain to be demonstrated.
The company witnessed revenue growth of 10.8% to Rs. 1,845.3 crore in FY2026, supported by the recovery in export
formulations, healthy growth in the Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient (API) business and improved revenues from Warren
Remedies Private Limited. Export formulation revenues grew by 28.7% during the year, driven by growth of 14.4% in regulated
markets and 65.5% in non-regulated markets. The recovery in export formulations was also supported by the partial
resumption of operations at Goa Plant II after the United States Food and Drug Administration (USFDA) permitted the company
to restart production on two of its four production lines by July 2025. The operational lines enabled supplies of select injectable
and ophthalmic products, in turn supporting recovery in margins to an extent. However, IRL’s margins and earnings remain far
below previous levels.

Source passage:
The recovery continued in Q1 FY2027, with operating income rising by 6.0% YoY to Rs. 467.5 crore, supported by growth in the
US and API businesses.
The operating margin improved to 7.7% in FY2026 from 6.0% in FY2025, supported by the recovery in export sales and cost-
optimisation measures implemented under the MMP. The MMP enabled larger batch sizes, increased automation and reduced
manual intervention, thereby improving productivity and lowering per-unit manufacturing and testing costs. Workforce
rationalisation and other efficiencies under the MMP, is expected to generate annual savings of Rs. 14-15 crore. The
improvement continued in Q1 FY2027, with the operating margin growing to 8.8% from 4.0% in Q1 FY2026, supported by the
recovery in export sales and operating efficiencies from the MMP. However, the extent and sustainability of further margin
improvement remains to be seen, given elevated raw material costs amid geopolitical uncertainties, suboptimal utilisation of
Goa Plant II, and continued advertising and brand building expenditure at Warren Remedies Private Limited.
ICRA notes that the company has undertaken asset monetisation and working capital management initiatives to improve
liquidity. IRL received around Rs. 100 crore from the monetisation of its ophthalmic business and a cash inflow of around Rs.
64 crore from the sale of a land parcel in Mumbai in H1 FY2027. These proceeds, along with improved collections and scheduled
repayments, supported a reduction in consolidated debt in the recent months. However, the liquidity position remains
sensitive to the company’s ability to sustain operating cash flows amid a rising raw material price environment and contain its
working capital borrowings.
IRL’s financial risk profile remains constrained by elevated leverage and weak coverage indicators. Total debt stood at
Rs. 1,084.2 crore as on March 31, 2026, while total debt/OPBDITA remained high at 7.6 times. Interest coverage and DSCR
were weak at 1.2 times and 0.7 times, respectively, in FY2026. Further, working capital intensity remained moderately high at
34.6%, reflecting longer receivable cycles in export markets and sizeable inventory requirements. Although the anticipated
recovery in earnings and scheduled debt repayments could support a gradual improvement in credit metrics, the pace and
sustainability of deleveraging remain key monitorables.

Goa Plant II. The USFDA inspection conducted during August 27–September 4, 2026 resulted in seven Form 483 observations.

Statement:
ICRA has considered the consolidated financials of IRL for arriving at the ratings.

Source passage:
Rating sensitivities
Positive factors – The outlook may be revised to Stable in case the company demonstrates significant improvement in its
margins, leading to sustained improvement in its debt metrics, return indicators and liquidity position.
Negative factors – The rating may be downgraded if the company is unable to improve its revenues and margins materially by
scaling the additional capacities built over the last three years, leading to further weakening in the company’s overall financial
profile. Delays in resolution of existing regulatory non-compliance or any other regulatory non-compliance, thereby impacting
its product launches and, thus, revenues and profitability, would also be a negative rating trigger.
Analytical approach
Analytical approach | Comments
Applicable rating methodologies | Corporate Credit Rating Methodology Pharmaceuticals
Parent/Group support | Not applicable
Consolidation/Standalone | For arriving at the ratings, ICRA has considered the consolidated financials of IRL (see Annexure II for details).
About the company
Indoco Remedies Limited was established by Mr. Govind Ramnath Kare in 1947 as Indo Continental Trading
Company and was involved in imports of pharmaceutical formulations from Europe and their sales in India. In 1963,
the current Chairman, Mr. Suresh G. Kare took over. At present, IRL manufactures and markets branded
formulations and APIs, and is engaged in providing contract research and manufacturing services (CRAMS) with a
strong presence in domestic formulations, which contributed to around 44.3% of its total revenues in FY2026
(consolidated). In the domestic business, IRL has a prominent presence in the anti-infective, respiratory, gastro-
intestinal and dental segments.
The export formulations business comprised 39% of IRL’s revenues in FY2026 while APIs accounted for 9% in FY2026
with the balance derived from contract research and analytics. IRL’s formulations plants are located at Goa (three
plants), Waluj (Aurangabad, Maharashtra) and Baddi (Himachal Pradesh; two plants), while API units are located at
Patalganga (Maharashtra) and Rabale (Navi Mumbai). In FY2017, IRL acquired Micro Labs Limited’s solid oral dosage
manufacturing facility at Baddi, which is being utilised to manufacture formulations for the European and the UK
markets. Overall, IRL has 10 manufacturing facilities in India, six for finished dosages and four for APIs, supported
by an R&D centre, a Clinical Research Organization (CRO) and a Global Stability Centre. The company’s
manufacturing facilities are approved by various regulatory authorities including USFDA, UK-MHRA and TGA-
Australia. In FY2025, the company established a wholly-owned subsidiary, Warren Remedies Private Limited, to
enter the OTC segment.
Key financial indicators (audited)
Indoco Remedies Limited (Consolidated)
[TABLE: FY2025 | FY2026]
Operating income | FY2025: 1,664.9 | FY2026: 1,845.3
PAT | FY2025: (78.0) | FY2026: (98.7)
OPBDIT/OI | FY2025: 6.0% | FY2026: 7.7%
PAT/OI | FY2025: -4.7% | FY2026: -5.3%
[/TABLE]

respective categories. The established brand portfolio and wide therapeutic coverage support the stability of the domestic

supported by volume growth, improved retail availability, price increases and healthy contribution from new product launches,

demand volatility, regulatory developments or supply disruptions in any single market. Going forward, the revenue profile is
expected to remain diversified, supported by stable growth in the domestic business and a gradual recovery across key export
markets following the normalisation of supplies and completion of major plant upgradation under the MMP.

larger batch sizes, automation and workforce rationalisation are expected to improve productivity, reduce per-unit

lines and improving the utilisation and profitability of the facility. Any delay in regulatory closure or fresh adverse regulatory
action could constrain product approvals, exports and profitability.

scaling the additional capacities built over the last three years, leading to further weakening in the company’s overall financial
profile. Delays in resolution of existing regulatory non-compliance or any other regulatory non-compliance, thereby impacting
its product launches and, thus, revenues and profitability, would also be a negative rating trigger.

About the company
Indoco Remedies Limited was established by Mr. Govind Ramnath Kare in 1947 as Indo Continental Trading
Company and was involved in imports of pharmaceutical formulations from Europe and their sales in India. In 1963,
the current Chairman, Mr. Suresh G. Kare took over. At present, IRL manufactures and markets branded
formulations and APIs, and is engaged in providing contract research and manufacturing services (CRAMS) with a
strong presence in domestic formulations, which contributed to around 44.3% of its total revenues in FY2026
(consolidated). In the domestic business, IRL has a prominent presence in the anti-infective, respiratory, gastro-
intestinal and dental segments.
The export formulations business comprised 39% of IRL’s revenues in FY2026 while APIs accounted for 9% in FY2026
with the balance derived from contract research and analytics. IRL’s formulations plants are located at Goa (three
plants), Waluj (Aurangabad, Maharashtra) and Baddi (Himachal Pradesh; two plants), while API units are located at
Patalganga (Maharashtra) and Rabale (Navi Mumbai). In FY2017, IRL acquired Micro Labs Limited’s solid oral dosage
manufacturing facility at Baddi, which is being utilised to manufacture formulations for the European and the UK
markets. Overall, IRL has 10 manufacturing facilities in India, six for finished dosages and four for APIs, supported
by an R&D centre, a Clinical Research Organization (CRO) and a Global Stability Centre. The company’s
manufacturing facilities are approved by various regulatory authorities including USFDA, UK-MHRA and TGA-
Australia. In FY2025, the company established a wholly-owned subsidiary, Warren Remedies Private Limited, to
enter the OTC segment.

messages.content:
Statement:
Creditor days increased to 198 days in FY2026 from 141 days in FY2025.

Source passage:
Elevated working capital intensity of operations – IRL’s working capital intensity remained moderately high at 34.6% in
FY2026; although it moderated from 37.7% in FY2025 following improved inventory movement and the gradual normalisation
of operations. The company’s export formulations business remains working capital intensive owing to relatively long
receivable cycles, while sizeable inventory is maintained to manage procurement lead times and ensure continuity of
production. Nevertheless, inventory days declined to 124 days in FY2026 from 139 days in FY2025, reflecting improved product
movement and dispatches following the easing of plant-related disruptions. Creditor days increased to 198 days from 141 days
amid pressure on cash flows and delayed supplier payments. Subsequently, liquidity generated through asset monetisation
initiatives, along with improved collections, enabled the company to settle most creditors outstanding for more than 90 days
and reduce working capital borrowings. Going forward, working capital intensity is expected to remain moderately high as the
company continues to focus on export markets, with sustained improvement in collections and inventory management
remaining key monitorables.
Weak profitability and elevated debt levels constrain financial risk profile – IRL’s financial risk profile remains constrained by
subdued profitability, elevated debt levels and weak debt-protection metrics. Although the operating margin improved to 7.7%
in FY2026 from 6.0% in FY2025, it remained significantly below historical levels amid the suboptimal utilisation of Goa Plant II,
implementation of MMP, and continued losses at Warren Remedies Private Limited. Despite the improvement in operating
profit, the company’s net loss widened to Rs. 98.7 crore in FY2026 from Rs. 78.0 crore in FY2025, primarily because of elevated
depreciation and finance costs following the sizeable debt-funded capital expenditure (capex) incurred in the preceding years.
Warren Remedies also reported a higher loss before tax of Rs. 64.3 crore in FY2026 over Rs. 36.0 crore in FY2025, owing to
sustained advertising and brand-building expenditure, finance costs and depreciation associated with its new facilities, and
operating expenses at the API plant, where products remained under validation.
The company had undertaken sizeable capex in the preceding years towards capacity expansion, implementation of the MMP,
additional production lines at Goa Plant II, and the toothpaste and API manufacturing facilities of Warren Remedies. With the
completion of the major capacity expansion and plant upgradation projects by FY2026, the company does not envisage any
significant capex over the near term. The proposed expenditure in the current fiscal is expected to be restricted primarily to
essential maintenance, energy saving initiatives and boiler installations, which should limit incremental funding requirements.
Going forward, profitability is expected to improve gradually, supported by the recovery in margin accretive export sales,
higher capacity utilisation, larger batch sizes, automation, manpower rationalisation and better absorption of fixed overheads.
Environmental and social risks
Environmental considerations – The company is not exposed to any significant physical climate-related risks. However, it
remains susceptible to evolving and increasingly stringent environmental regulations, particularly with respect to waste
management and pollution control norms. Any non-compliance or tightening of such regulations could lead to higher operating
costs as well as increased costs for future capacity additions.
Social considerations – The company is exposed to elevated industry-wide social risks, primarily driven by stringent product
safety requirements and the associated risk of litigation.

Statement:
About 11%-13% of the domestic formulations business is subject to Government mandated pricing controls under the National List of Essential Medicines (NLEM).

Source passage:
2026, resulting in seven Form 483 observations. Timely and satisfactory resolution of the observations and receipt of the EIR
remain critical for resolving the regulatory overhang, securing new product approvals, ramping up the remaining production
lines and improving the utilisation and profitability of the facility. Any delay in regulatory closure or fresh adverse regulatory
action could constrain product approvals, exports and profitability.
Vulnerability to regulatory risks, raw material price and forex fluctuations – IRL’s operations remain exposed to regulatory
risks arising from heightened scrutiny by regulatory authorities across domestic and export markets. The domestic
formulations business to the tune of about 11%-13% is also subject to Government mandated pricing controls, as a portion of
the company’s product portfolio is covered under the National List of Essential Medicines (NLEM). Although these controls
have not materially affected profitability in the past, any adverse revision in Government pricing policies could constrain pricing
flexibility and exert pressure on the domestic formulations business. The company’s profitability also remains vulnerable to
fluctuations in raw material, packaging and freight costs, with the impact on margins remaining a key monitorable. Further,
despite the use of forward contracts, IRL remains exposed to foreign exchange (forex) fluctuations arising from its overseas
operations and foreign currency borrowings. IRL also capitalises development expenditure incurred on Abbreviated New Drug
Applications (ANDAs), Drug Master Files and dossiers. Consequently, higher-than-anticipated price erosion, delays in
commercialisation or lower-than-expected returns from the related products could result in impairment of intangible assets.

# Indoco Remedies (NSE:INDOCO): What Did Management Reveal in Q1 FY27 Earnings Call?

- URL: https://www.kalkine.co.in/article/announcements/indoco-remedies-nseindoco-what-did-management-reveal-in-q1-fy27-earnings-call
- Published: 2026-08-04
- Fetched: 2026-10-25

You are reading a free article with opinions that may differ from the recommendation given by Kalkine in its paid research reports. Become a Kalkine member today to get access to our research reports, in-depth technical and fundamental research. Learn More

Indoco Remedies Limited (NSE:INDOCO) filed the transcript of its Q1 FY27 earnings conference call on 4 August 2026, covering the unaudited standalone and consolidated financial results for the quarter ended 30 June 2026. The call was held on 28 July 2026 and featured the Managing Director, Joint Managing Director, and CFO.

Standalone operational revenue grew 5.8% year-on-year to INR4,081 million in Q1 FY27, while consolidated revenue rose 8.2% to INR4,662 million.

Standalone EBITDA margin expanded sharply to 10.3% (INR422 million) in Q1 FY27 from 3.8% (INR148 million) in Q1 FY26.

US business revenues surged 62.2% year-on-year to INR459 million, and API revenues grew 42.4% to INR521 million during the quarter.

Baddi Unit III received EU-GMP certification from the German Health Authority, and Indoco Stability Center completed a USFDA pre-approval inspection with zero observations.

Indoco Remedies Limited (NSE:INDOCO), headquartered in Mumbai, is a fully integrated pharmaceutical company engaged in manufacturing and marketing formulations and active pharmaceutical ingredients (API). The company operates manufacturing facilities in Goa, Baddi, and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, serving domestic and international markets including the US, Europe, and South Africa, and is listed in the Pharma sector.

During Q1 FY27, domestic formulations revenues were INR2,040 million, broadly flat against INR2,028 million in Q1 FY26. International formulations grew 2.8% to INR1,451 million, with regulated markets up 19.3% to INR1,133 million. US revenues rose 62.2% to INR459 million, while Europe grew 2.5% to INR650 million. Emerging markets declined to INR317 million from INR461 million, attributed by management to timing-related primary billing in the prior March quarter.

The API segment grew 42.4% to INR521 million. The CRO and analytical solutions business, comprising AnaCipher CRO and Indoco Analytical Solutions, grew 36.2% to INR69 million. Management also disclosed the divestment of the Ophthalmic Division in India and agreed territories in Africa, described as a step to sharpen focus on core therapeutic areas. No update on outstanding USFDA plant matters was available at the time of the call.

and ophthalmology. The segment also benefited from extension of lifespan for some of its legacy products such as Cital-PM6
solution, Nosic OD, and Ezetrol in Q1 FY2026. Going forward, the domestic market is expected to render stable revenue growth
for IRL in FY2026 and FY2027, supported by its strong market position in respective therapy segments.
Healthy geographic diversification – In FY2025 and Q1 FY2026, although the company witnessed a revenue decline in export
formulations, it was partially offset by revenue growth in domestic formulations. IRL derived around 90% of its sales revenue
in Q1 FY2026 from the formulation segment, with 53% of the segment’s revenues generated by domestic markets and the rest
from export markets. The company has a strong domestic presence, with its major brands positioned among the top five in
respective therapy segments. In terms of export markets, regulated markets such as the US, Europe, South Africa, Australia
and New Zealand generated 68% of its export formulation revenues, while the rest came from the emerging markets. Going
forward, the revenues are expected to remain diversified, with stable growth from domestic markets and an expected gradual
revival in revenues from key export markets.
Credit challenges
Pending resolution of OAI status from the USFDA for IRL’s Goa Plants II and III – IRL’s Goa Plants II and III were inspected by
USFDA in February 2023 and received their OAI status in June 2023. While IRL was working on the remediation, USFDA audited
the facility again in February 2024 and a warning letter was issued to the site in December 2024. IRL is working on remediating
the same, and its US revenues from the site were impacted to some extent due to the ongoing refurbishment. USFDA has given
approval for resumption of production for two lines of the four at the Goa Plant II recently. ICRA notes that the manufacturing
facility for Oral Solid Dosage (OSD) at Goa Plant I continues to remain Current Good Manufacturing Practice (CGMP) compliant
and supply to the US continues from this site. Going forward, any new Abbreviated New Drug Application (ANDA) filings from
the facility will be approved only when the OAI status is resolved and, hence, timely resolution of the same remains a key
monitorable.
Vulnerability to regulatory risks, raw material price and foreign exchange fluctuations – The company’s operations remain
exposed to regulatory risks due to increased scrutiny by the regulatory agencies and pricing controls in the domestic market.
ICRA notes that the company derives some revenues from products under the National List of Essential Medicines (NLEM) but
draws comfort from the fact that the same has not materially impacted its profit margins. Nevertheless, any adverse changes
in Government price policies could lead to pricing pressures and affect the company’s domestic formulations business. IRL’s
profitability is also vulnerable to fluctuations in raw material, packaging and freight costs and their impact on margins will
remain a key monitorable. The company’s margins also remain vulnerable to foreign exchange fluctuations due to its overseas
operations and foreign currency borrowings despite hedging through forward contracts. ICRA notes that IRL capitalises
development expenditures for ANDAs/Drug Master Files (DMFs)/dossiers and any higher-than-expected price erosion or
lower-than-expected returns, exposes the company to the risk of impairment of intangibles.

Statement:
Working capital intensity remained moderately high at 34.6% in FY2026.

Source passage:
Elevated working capital intensity of operations – IRL’s working capital intensity remained moderately high at 34.6% in
FY2026; although it moderated from 37.7% in FY2025 following improved inventory movement and the gradual normalisation
of operations. The company’s export formulations business remains working capital intensive owing to relatively long
receivable cycles, while sizeable inventory is maintained to manage procurement lead times and ensure continuity of
production. Nevertheless, inventory days declined to 124 days in FY2026 from 139 days in FY2025, reflecting improved product
movement and dispatches following the easing of plant-related disruptions. Creditor days increased to 198 days from 141 days
amid pressure on cash flows and delayed supplier payments. Subsequently, liquidity generated through asset monetisation
initiatives, along with improved collections, enabled the company to settle most creditors outstanding for more than 90 days
and reduce working capital borrowings. Going forward, working capital intensity is expected to remain moderately high as the
company continues to focus on export markets, with sustained improvement in collections and inventory management
remaining key monitorables.
Weak profitability and elevated debt levels constrain financial risk profile – IRL’s financial risk profile remains constrained by
subdued profitability, elevated debt levels and weak debt-protection metrics. Although the operating margin improved to 7.7%
in FY2026 from 6.0% in FY2025, it remained significantly below historical levels amid the suboptimal utilisation of Goa Plant II,
implementation of MMP, and continued losses at Warren Remedies Private Limited. Despite the improvement in operating
profit, the company’s net loss widened to Rs. 98.7 crore in FY2026 from Rs. 78.0 crore in FY2025, primarily because of elevated
depreciation and finance costs following the sizeable debt-funded capital expenditure (capex) incurred in the preceding years.
Warren Remedies also reported a higher loss before tax of Rs. 64.3 crore in FY2026 over Rs. 36.0 crore in FY2025, owing to
sustained advertising and brand-building expenditure, finance costs and depreciation associated with its new facilities, and
operating expenses at the API plant, where products remained under validation.
The company had undertaken sizeable capex in the preceding years towards capacity expansion, implementation of the MMP,
additional production lines at Goa Plant II, and the toothpaste and API manufacturing facilities of Warren Remedies. With the
completion of the major capacity expansion and plant upgradation projects by FY2026, the company does not envisage any
significant capex over the near term. The proposed expenditure in the current fiscal is expected to be restricted primarily to
essential maintenance, energy saving initiatives and boiler installations, which should limit incremental funding requirements.
Going forward, profitability is expected to improve gradually, supported by the recovery in margin accretive export sales,
higher capacity utilisation, larger batch sizes, automation, manpower rationalisation and better absorption of fixed overheads.
Environmental and social risks
Environmental considerations – The company is not exposed to any significant physical climate-related risks. However, it
remains susceptible to evolving and increasingly stringent environmental regulations, particularly with respect to waste
management and pollution control norms. Any non-compliance or tightening of such regulations could lead to higher operating
costs as well as increased costs for future capacity additions.
Social considerations – The company is exposed to elevated industry-wide social risks, primarily driven by stringent product
safety requirements and the associated risk of litigation.

    definition: Total borrowings (short and long term, including current maturities) plus lease liabilities (current and non-current) minus cash and bank balances minus liquid investments (current investments only), all at the latest audited year end on the consolidated basis when consolidated statements exist (policy section 4).
    derive_from: total borrowings; lease liabilities; cash and bank balances; liquid investments
    component 'total borrowings': all borrowings, short-term plus long-term, including the current maturities of long-term borrowings; lease liabilities are a separate component
    component 'lease liabilities': lease liabilities, current plus non-current (add both parts; use one total only when that is all the documents give)
    component 'cash and bank balances': cash and cash equivalents plus other bank balances (including bank deposits) under current assets
    component 'liquid investments': current investments only: mutual funds, treasury bills and fixed deposits shown under current assets; never non-current investments or investments in subsidiaries, associates or joint ventures

You are a credit officer writing section 3 of a credit review.

From the verified facts and score results supplied by the user, produce at most 8 short
inferences a credit officer would draw about the borrower. Cover the important trends, risks,
and repayment capacity; do not repeat a fact verbatim as an inference.

Every inference must have:
- opinion: one sentence stating the judgement.
- fact_ids: the ids of the verified facts the judgement rests on. Use only ids from the list.
- reasoning: two to four sentences that reference only those facts. Do not introduce outside
  knowledge, management guidance, market assumptions, or unlisted numbers.
- When the reasoning quotes a ratio the company itself reports (interest coverage, DSCR, net
  debt/EBITDA, current ratio, debt/equity), say it is the company-reported figure, state its
  basis if the source gives one (consolidated or standalone, and how it is defined), and never
  present it as the policy ratio, which the policy rules compute separately.
- confidence: a number from 0 to 1 reflecting the strength of the evidence.
- quantitative: true only when the judgement is an arithmetic or threshold comparison that can
  be checked in Lean.

For a quantitative inference also include lean_claim:
- facts: an object mapping each Lean variable name used in the claim to the fact that
  supplies its value, for example {"net_debt": "F012", "ebitda": "F013"}. A plain fact id
  uses the fact's first listed number; to use another number of that fact write the id, a
  hash sign and the number exactly as listed, for example "F046#1.25" for the 1.25 times
  covenant limit of F046, whose first number 1.78 is the actual ratio. Two variables must
  never name the same number.
- claim: a closed integer arithmetic statement over those variable names, written with
  comparison operators such as <=, <, >=, > or ==, for example "2 * net_debt <= 7 * ebitda".
  A whole side of a comparison that is a bare integer, such as the 1 in
  "interest_coverage < 1" or the 0 in "net_loss < 0", is read in the natural unit of the other
  side: crore for money (never lakh), percent for percentages, times for ratios.
  Never write a decimal literal such as 1.25: map that number to a variable instead (every
  threshold you compare against must come from a fact). Do not use division, functions,
  hypotheses, or variable names that are not keys in facts. Write a comparison chain as separate
  comparisons joined by &&, never "a < b < c". All variables compared with each other must be
  in the same unit (do not compare a crore amount with a ratio or a percentage).

Return JSON with one key, inferences, holding the list of inference objects. Order the most
important inferences first and use no more than 8.

Reply with one JSON value only, minified on a single line: no indentation, no line breaks between tokens, no prose, no Markdown code fences. The value must conform to this JSON schema:
{"$defs":{"InferenceDraft":{"description":"One LLM-written inference before code validation and Lean quantification.","properties":{"opinion":{"default":"","title":"Opinion","type":"string"},"fact_ids":{"items":{"type":"string"},"title":"Fact Ids","type":"array"},"reasoning":{"default":"","title":"Reasoning","type":"string"},"confidence":{"default":0.5,"title":"Confidence","type":"number"},"quantitative":{"default":false,"title":"Quantitative","type":"boolean"},"lean_claim":{"anyOf":[{"$ref":"#/$defs/LeanClaim"},{"type":"null"}],"default":null}},"title":"InferenceDraft","type":"object"},"LeanClaim":{"description":"A Lean sketch mapping variable names to fact ids and an arithmetic claim.","properties":{"facts":{"additionalProperties":{"type":"string"},"title":"Facts","type":"object"},"claim":{"default":"","title":"Claim","type":"string"}},"title":"LeanClaim","type":"object"}},"description":"The inference writer's structured reply.","properties":{"inferences":{"items":{"$ref":"#/$defs/InferenceDraft"},"title":"Inferences","type":"array"}},"title":"InferenceOutput","type":"object"}

Score: internal_risk_grade. Input: major_red_flag_count (count).
Definition: Number of major red flags present under policy section 6
value is a whole number, the count of distinct major red flags the facts evidence.

Policy rubric:
6. Red flags
Each of the following is a **major red flag**; two or more is a mandatory referral to the
credit committee and one raises the Internal Risk Grade by one notch (section 9):

1. Qualified or adverse audit opinion, disclaimer of opinion, or emphasis of matter on going
   concern.
2. Any delay of more than 30 days in debt servicing in the last 24 months (SMA-1 or worse).
3. Promoter pledge above 50 percent of promoter holding.
4. Material litigation or regulatory proceedings (claim or penalty above 10 percent of net
   worth) that is not provided for.
5. Auditor resignation before the end of the term without reasons, or change of statutory
   auditor twice in 3 years.
6. Related-party transactions with advances or loans to promoter entities above 10 percent
   of net worth.
7. Material negative adverse media regarding fraud, forensic audit or investigation by an
   enforcement agency.

- score_id=financial_strength_score slot=net_debt unit='INR crore x 100': Total borrowings less cash, bank balances and liquid investments, latest audited year
    definition: Total borrowings (short and long term, including current maturities) plus lease liabilities (current and non-current) minus cash and bank balances minus liquid investments (current investments only), all at the latest audited year end on the consolidated basis when consolidated statements exist (policy section 4).
    derive_from: total borrowings; lease liabilities; cash and bank balances; liquid investments
    component 'total borrowings': all borrowings, short-term plus long-term, including the current maturities of long-term borrowings; lease liabilities are a separate component
    component 'lease liabilities': lease liabilities, current plus non-current (add both parts; use one total only when that is all the documents give)
    component 'cash and bank balances': cash and cash equivalents plus other bank balances (including bank deposits) under current assets
    component 'liquid investments': current investments only: mutual funds, treasury bills and fixed deposits shown under current assets; never non-current investments or investments in subsidiaries, associates or joint ventures
- score_id=maximum_exposure slot=tangible_net_worth unit='INR crore x 100': Tangible net worth at year end
    definition: Shareholders' equity (net worth) minus intangible assets (goodwill, other intangibles and intangibles under development) at the latest audited year end (policy section 2).
    derive_from: total_equity; intangible assets
    component 'total_equity': shareholders' equity (net worth) at the year end
    component 'intangible assets': goodwill, other intangible assets and intangible assets under development at the year end

Upon conclusion of the inspection, the USFDA issued seven observations in Form 483.

Indoco Remedies said it is addressing the observations comprehensively and will submit its response to the USFDA within the stipulated timeframe.

Also Read: Indoco Remedies Secures EU GMP Certification for Goa Manufacturing Plant

Form 483 observations are issued by USFDA investigators when they identify conditions or practices that may indicate violations of regulatory requirements during an inspection. The issuance of Form 483 does not, by itself, represent a final regulatory determination.

Indoco Remedies Limited is a fully integrated, research-oriented pharmaceutical company headquartered in Mumbai, with a presence in international markets. According to the company's official information, it operates 11 manufacturing facilities, including seven for finished dosage forms (FDFs) and four for active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), supported by a research and development centre and a clinical research organisation (CRO) facility. Its manufacturing facilities have received approvals from several regulatory authorities, including the USFDA and UK-MHRA. The company develops and manufactures a range of pharmaceutical products for the Indian and international markets and has a portfolio spanning therapeutic segments including gastro-intestinal, respiratory, anti-infectives, ophthalmic, cardiovascular, anti-diabetic, pain management and gynaecology.

Also Read: USFDA successfully completes inspection at Indoco Remedies Mumbai API facility

Revenue Recognition
The company derives major portion of its revenue from manufacturing and marketing of Formulations
(Finished Dosage Forms) and Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs). Other sources of revenue
include Dossiers development, Analytical Studies and Bio-equivalent studies undertaken by the
company on behalf of customers.
With effect from April 1, 2018, the company has adopted Ind AS 115, Revenue from Contracts with
Customers. The company analysed the impact of Ind AS on incomplete contracts, if any and concluded
that the effect of adoption of Ind AS 115 was insignificant.
Recognising revenue from major business activities
i.
Sale of goods – FDF and API
Revenue from sale of FDF and API are recognised when the performance obligations are satisfied
in accordance with Ind AS 115. Performance obligations are deemed to have been satisfied when
substantial risk and rewards of ownership are transferred to the customer and the customer obtains
control of the promised goods. In case of domestic sales, performance obligations are satisfied
when goods are dispatched, or delivery is handed over to the transporter. In case of export sales,
performance obligations are satisfied based on terms defined in the contracts. In case of Ex-works
contracts, performance obligation is satisfied when goods are shipped or dispatched from the
factory and in other cases when the goods are shipped on board based on Bill of Lading / Airway
Bill or any other similar document evidencing delivery thereof.
ii.
Revenue from services
Services provided include Dossiers development, Analytical Studies and Bio- equivalent studies
undertaken by the company on behalf of customers.
The contracts with customers for Dossiers and study reports are fixed-price contracts. Revenue
from such contracts, where the performance obligations are satisfied over time and where there
is no significant uncertainty as to measurement or collectability of consideration, is recognised
based on the terms agreed with the customers.
Estimates of revenues, costs or extent of progress toward completion are revised if circumstances
change. The effect that the contract modification has on the transaction price, and on the entity’s
measure of progress towards complete satisfaction of the performance obligation, is recognised
as an adjustment to revenue (either as an increase in or a reduction of revenue) at the date of the
contract modification (i.e. the adjustment to revenue is made on a cumulative catch-up basis).
iii.	 Other operating revenue - Export incentives
Revenue from Export Incentives under various schemes is recognised when the performance
obligations are satisfied i.e. when the related export sales are effected.
iv.	 Sales Return
The Company recognises provision for sales return, on the basis of past experience, measured
on net basis of the margin of the sales. Any unutilised provision for sales return is reversed to the
Statement of Profit and Loss on completion of 3 years from the date of creation.
f.
Government Grants
Grants from the government are recognised at their fair value where there is reasonable assurance that
the grant will be received and the Company will comply with all attached conditions.
Government grants relating to the purchase of property, plant and equipment are included in non-
current liabilities as deferred income and are credited to Profit and Loss on a straight - line basis over

the expected lives of related assets and presented within other income.

Passages:
[D5:p1:c1]
Upon conclusion of the inspection, the USFDA issued seven observations in Form 483.

Indoco Remedies said it is addressing the observations comprehensively and will submit its response to the USFDA within the stipulated timeframe.

Also Read: Indoco Remedies Secures EU GMP Certification for Goa Manufacturing Plant

Form 483 observations are issued by USFDA investigators when they identify conditions or practices that may indicate violations of regulatory requirements during an inspection. The issuance of Form 483 does not, by itself, represent a final regulatory determination.

Indoco Remedies Limited is a fully integrated, research-oriented pharmaceutical company headquartered in Mumbai, with a presence in international markets. According to the company's official information, it operates 11 manufacturing facilities, including seven for finished dosage forms (FDFs) and four for active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), supported by a research and development centre and a clinical research organisation (CRO) facility. Its manufacturing facilities have received approvals from several regulatory authorities, including the USFDA and UK-MHRA. The company develops and manufactures a range of pharmaceutical products for the Indian and international markets and has a portfolio spanning therapeutic segments including gastro-intestinal, respiratory, anti-infectives, ophthalmic, cardiovascular, anti-diabetic, pain management and gynaecology.

Mumbai: Indoco Remedies Limited has received seven observations in Form 483 following a US Food and Drug Administration (USFDA) inspection of its Plant II (Sterile) manufacturing facility in Goa.

The inspection was conducted from August 27 to September 4, 2026, at the company's Plant II (Sterile) facility in Goa. Upon conclusion of the inspection, the USFDA issued seven observations in Form 483.

Indoco Remedies said it is addressing the observations comprehensively and will submit its response to the USFDA within the stipulated timeframe.
